summary: A HUD navigation system application for astronauts in the planet Mars. It is an interface that shows the 3D globe or 2D views which contains automatized route planning taking account of hazards like crater rims, steep slopes and customized hazards.
details:
This is an application service that requires a web navigator so that the user can interact with it. It is a navigation system where you can plan a route, and it can be done by either picking points on the map or searching by georeferenced point names, and it computes it using gathered data from USGS and NASA missions done in Mars. You can simulate how the route looks like when the astronaut is going through it.

The application allows the user to choose layers of the planet surface images and georeferencing points. It has some POVs like following camera and route overview. There is a "settings" window where the user can customize the navigation system, POV system, route planning and online hazard data fetched behavior. There is a telemetry tab and traverse progress widget.

The system aims to help astronauts navigate safely through the Martian environment by integrating thermal, spectral, topographic, geophysical, atmospheric, radiation, and chemical information. It will feature two complementary interfaces: an interactive map displayed inside the spacecraft or habitat for mission planning and route assessment, and a Heads-Up Display (HUD) available on a portable tablet or projected onto the spacesuit helmet visor, providing astronauts with essential environmental information and navigation guidance during surface exploration.

The developed code was done with the help of Claude AI, and it was developed in HTML and Javascript. APIs and SDKs from ArcGIS, ESRI, NASA's Mars trek have been used to retrieve and integrate the information required for each route planning, visualization so that it can show 2D and 3D visualization and information about georeferencing points and hazards.
